pr_title: Allocate IP address before running tests
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Ricardo Pchevuzinske Katz <ricardo.katz@gmail.com>


**What type of PR is this?**

/kind failing-test
/kind flake

**What this PR does / why we need it**: This PR allocates an IP address for the ingress before each test.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #94806 

**Special notes for your reviewer**: There are some thoughts in the original issue, about if this is the real root cause of the flake (a previous IP allocation has been removed from a test that would run later) of if there's something that changed in GCP or in the way IP addresses are allocated.

Otherwise I couldn't find other plausible reason for the flake

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```

🤖 I am a bot run by vllry. 👩‍🔬

It seems that the ingress is created successfully (per the api-server logs, the GET of the object returns a resp=200) but the test still does the GET for 10m until it fails:
```
I0915 06:46:33.713196       8 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="POST" URI="/apis/networking.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/ingress-5967/ingresses" latency="7.055502ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/37cf1d6 -- [sig-network] Loadbalancing: L7 GCE [Slow] [Feature:NEG] should conform to Ingress spec" srcIP="35.192.111.110:48138" resp=201
[...]
I0915 06:56:38.362318       8 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="DELETE" URI="/apis/networking.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/ingress-5967/ingresses/echomap" latency="7.920863ms" userAgent="e2e.test/v1.20.0 (linux/amd64) kubernetes/37cf1d6 -- [sig-network] Loadbalancing: L7 GCE [Slow] [Feature:NEG] should conform to Ingress spec" srcIP="35.192.111.110:48138" resp=200
```
Per the GCP resources it's hard to know if an IP Address has been allocated to the ingress (maybe some regex problem) or if this is some other problem.

I have almost none knowledge of e2e tests and GCP environment (need some help, probably from @bowei) but I would like to follow this issue to know how to solve this sort of thing. I'll keep investigating here the upper layers to see what it expects and why it gets this error. Maybe it's allocating a non-expected IP Address

One additional error from the logs, it really seems the Ingress is being created without address:

```
Namespace:        ingress-5967
Address:          
``` 
Maybe something specific from the cluster, some permission or from the way the ingress is being created.

The previous commit removed a GCE IP allocation: 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/deffddbfb5466d4b1fefd9f955646426b2613c80#diff-ae2588ed31c4a644d59d239e3ed191dfL140

 but this seems to be related to HTTPs tests.

My question here is, if the tests run parallelized (do they?) the first go fails and the next ones succeeds because there's an IP address allocated. 

As far as I've read from GCP it creates an IP Address based in the existence of an IngressClass annotation (even if this was deprecated, I think) so probably no IP is being allocated and the test suite needs to be changed to remove the annotation or to contain the IngressClass specification to GKE.

And maybe the NEG tests were already passing because there was a spare IP address? I don't know how NEG works inside GCP, by the docs it doesn't needs the annotation anymore.

So my guess is:
* The missing IP address allocation might be something missing
* If not the IP address, probably how the ingress is being created.

I'll open a PR to allocate an IP address BeforeEach test, and see if this deflakes. Don't know if this is the expected behavior in GCP but it seems there are other cases this allocation happens.

No problem :)

I'll leave this as triage/unresolved for tomorrow sig-network meeting so when triaging the issues it will got some attention from GCE folks also and they can provide some better feedback. 

As this is a periodic job I don't know how to force it to run with the PR, so now just need to wait for some review :)
